questions.question: How many censuses had been completed in India as of year 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **15** censuses had been completed in India as of the year 2011.
 
• The census in India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, but the first complete census was taken in 1881.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country.
 
• The census provides critical data on population demographics, economic activity, literacy and education, housing and household amenities, urbanization, fertility and mortality, and many other socio-economic characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Census** is one of the most reliable sources of data on various demographic and socio-economic parameters.
 
• It helps in planning and formulation of policies for the government at all levels.
 
• The Census of India 2011 was conducted in two phases: the House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010) and the Population Enumeration (9th to 28th February 2011).
 
• India's census is the largest administrative exercise in the world, covering all individuals residing in the country.
 
• The next census was scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) Though India has a federal system, the Constitution does not mention the word ‘federation’.

2) Article 5 of the Constitution says that the Parliament by law can create a new state.

3) On the subjects in the Union list, each State Legislature can enact laws for the State.

4) Both the Parliament and State Legislature can pass laws on subjects in concurrent list.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 and 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 2:** Article 5 of the Constitution does not pertain to the creation of new states. It deals with the citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. The power to create new states is vested in Parliament under Article 3.
 
• **Statement 3:** The subjects in the Union List are exclusively under the purview of the Union Parliament. State Legislatures cannot enact laws on subjects in the Union List.
 
• Since both statements 2 and 3 are incorrect, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement 1:** It is correct that the Constitution of India does not use the word 'federation' but describes India as a 'Union of States'.
 
• **Statement 4:** Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can indeed pass laws on subjects listed in the Concurrent List, with the central law prevailing in case of conflict.
 
• The Constitution of India is a comprehensive document that lays down the framework for governance and the distribution of powers between the Union and the States.

questions.question: Under which Gharana do the composition of blend of Khayal and Dhrupad-Dhamar styles come?

__
 
• The **Agra Gharana** is known for its blend of Khayal and Dhrupad-Dhamar styles.
 
• This Gharana emphasizes the importance of swara (notes) and laya (tempo) in its compositions.
 
• It has a rich history and has contributed significantly to Hindustani classical music.
 
• The compositions from this Gharana often feature intricate and robust patterns.
 
• Famous exponents of the Agra Gharana include Faiyaz Khan and Vilayat Hussain Khan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indore Gharana** is known for its unique style of Khayal singing and was popularized by Ustad Amir Khan.
 
• The **Gwalior Gharana** is one of the oldest Khayal Gharanas and emphasizes the use of simple and straightforward compositions.
 
• The **Patiala Gharana** is famous for its elaborate and intricate taans (fast melodic passages).
 
• Gharanas are schools or styles of music that are passed down through generations, each with its own distinct features and techniques.

questions.question: In MS-Word, a number printed above the base line is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**superscript**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A number printed above the base line in MS-Word is referred to as a **superscript**.
 
• Superscripts are often used in mathematical expressions, chemical formulas, and for footnotes or endnotes in documents.
 
• To apply superscript formatting in MS-Word, you can use the shortcut key **Ctrl + Shift + +** or use the Superscript button in the Font group on the Home tab.
 
• Examples of superscripts include 2ⁿd, x², and H₂O where the "2" is in a smaller, raised font above the baseline.
 
• Superscripts are different from subscripts, which are printed below the baseline and are used for different purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• MS-Word offers various text formatting options, including bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript, and superscript.
 
• Formatting text can enhance the readability and presentation of your document.
 
• Using the correct formatting options ensures that your document is clear and professional.

questions.question: What do you mean by semiconservative DNA replication?

options.text: RNA is dependent on DNA for the synthesis of proteins
After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.
After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have two parental and two newly synthesised strand.
DNA is dependent on RNA for the synthesis of proteins

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Semiconservative DNA replication** means that after the completion of replication, each DNA molecule consists of one parental (original) strand and one newly synthesized strand.
 
• This model of DNA replication was first proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953 and later confirmed by the Meselson-Stahl experiment in 1958.
 
• The semiconservative nature ensures genetic consistency through generations, as each new DNA molecule retains one strand from the original DNA.
 
• This mechanism is crucial for the accurate transmission of genetic information during cell division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA replication** is a fundamental process that occurs in all living organisms to copy their DNA, allowing for cell division and reproduction.
 
• There are three main hypotheses for DNA replication: conservative, semiconservative, and dispersive. The semiconservative model is the one that has been experimentally validated.
 
• In the **Meselson-Stahl experiment**, E. coli bacteria were grown in a medium containing a heavy isotope of nitrogen (15N) and then transferred to a medium with a lighter isotope (14N). The results showed that after one round of replication, the DNA consisted of hybrid molecules (one strand 15N and one strand 14N), supporting the semiconservative model.
 
• This process ensures that the genetic material is accurately duplicated and passed on to daughter cells, maintaining the integrity of the genome.

questions.question: Indian Constitution came into force on ________ and is celebrated as Republic Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jan 26 1950 **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jan 26 1950 **is the date when the Indian Constitution came into force and is celebrated as Republic Day.
 
• The date marks the transition of India from a British Dominion to a republic, and the Constitution of India became the supreme law of the land.
 
• Republic Day is one of the three national holidays in India, along with Independence Day and Gandhi Jayanti.
 
• The main celebration takes place in the national capital, New Delhi, at the Rajpath before the President of India.
 
• The event includes a grand parade showcasing India's defense capability, cultural and social heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Name the digital payment platform launched in 2021 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in association with Department of Financial Services (DFS), National Health Authority (NHA) and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW).

• The platform is designed to deliver benefits and services to citizens in a seamless and efficient manner.
 
• e-RUPI is a QR code or SMS string-based e-voucher, which is delivered to the beneficiaries' mobile phones.
 
• Users can redeem the voucher without needing a card, digital payments app, or internet banking access.
 
• It ensures that the payment to the service provider is made only after the transaction is completed.
 
• The platform is aimed at improving the delivery of welfare services and ensuring leak-proof transactions.

• It was established in 2008 and is an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Indian Banks' Association (IBA).
 
• The NPCI aims to create infrastructure to handle the entire volume of retail payment systems in the country.
 
• e-RUPI is part of the Indian government's efforts to promote digital transactions and financial inclusion.
 
• The platform is expected to play a significant role in achieving the vision of a Digital India.

questions.question: The Green Revolution was due to the introduction of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high yielding varieties of seeds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** was primarily due to the introduction of **high yielding varieties of seeds**.
 
• This revolution started in the 1960s in India and significantly increased agricultural production, especially in wheat and rice.
 
• Other factors contributing to the Green Revolution included the use of fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques, but the high yielding varieties of seeds were the cornerstone.
 
• The main aim was to make India self-sufficient in food grains and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• The Green Revolution had a significant impact on food security and rural development in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was led by agricultural scientists like **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan** in India.
 
• It was part of a larger initiative supported by international organizations such as the **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** and the **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)**.
 
• The high yielding varieties of seeds were developed through cross-breeding and genetic modifications to increase resistance to pests and diseases.
 
• Although the Green Revolution had many benefits, it also led to environmental issues such as soil degradation, overuse of water resources, and increased use of chemical inputs.

questions.question: The colour of the surface of Mars is red because of the presence of large amounts of chemical compounds in it. What is the name of that compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron oxide**__

__
 
• The surface of Mars appears red due to the presence of large amounts of **Iron oxide**.
 
• Iron oxide is commonly known as rust, and its reddish color gives Mars its characteristic hue.
 
• Mars is often referred to as the "Red Planet" because of this distinctive coloration.
 
• The iron oxide particles are distributed across the Martian soil and dust, contributing to the planet's overall red appearance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mars** is the fourth planet from the Sun and is named after the Roman god of war.
 
• The planet has a thin atmosphere, composed mostly of carbon dioxide, with traces of nitrogen and argon.
 
• Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, and a canyon system, Valles Marineris, that dwarfs the Grand Canyon.
 
• Exploration missions to Mars aim to understand its geology, climate, and potential for past or present life.
 
• Recent missions include NASA's Perseverance rover, which is searching for signs of ancient microbial life and collecting samples for future return to Earth.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor to the Government of India in the year 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V Anantha Nageswaran**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **V Anantha Nageswaran** was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor to the Government of India in January 2022.
 
• He succeeded **Krishnamurthy Subramanian**, who completed his three-year term in December 2021.
 
• Nageswaran is an academic and former executive with a rich background in economic analysis and financial markets.
 
• He holds a doctoral degree from the University of Massachusetts in Amherst and has previously worked as a writer, teacher, and consultant.
 
• As the Chief Economic Advisor, Nageswaran is responsible for advising the government on economic matters and providing insights into policy decisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)** is a key position in the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• The CEA plays a crucial role in the preparation of the Economic Survey, which is presented before the Union Budget.
 
• The Economic Survey provides a detailed report on the state of the economy and outlines the policy challenges and solutions.
 
• Previous CEAs include prominent economists such as **Arvind Subramanian** and **Raghuram Rajan**.
 
• The position of CEA is instrumental in shaping the economic policy and direction of the country.
